title: Breakfast in Tehran
intro: It is Friday, the Iranian weekend, and Tom is invited to breakfast at Reza and Mina's flat. Fresh barbari bread, white cheese, walnuts, butter, honey and glasses of tea – but everyone at the table eats something different. The story practises food words, دوست داشتن 'to like' and می‌خواهد 'wants', and shows you a Persian word for a very Iranian kind of bite.
source: An original story for this course.

sentences.fa: رضا صبح زود به نانوایی می‌رود و نان بربری می‌خرد.
sentences.r: Rezā sobh-e zud be nānvāyi mi-ravad o nān-e barbari mi-kharad.
sentences.en: Early in the morning Reza goes to the bakery and buys barbari bread.

sentences.fa: تام هم امروز مهمان آن‌ها است.
sentences.r: Tām ham emruz mehmān-e ān-hā ast.
sentences.en: Today Tom is their guest too.

sentences.fa: روی سفره نان، پنیر، گردو، کره و عسل هست.
sentences.r: ru-ye sofre nān, panir, gerdu, kare o 'asal hast.
sentences.en: On the sofreh there is bread, cheese, walnuts, butter and honey.

sentences.fa: رضا نان و پنیر و گردو می‌خورد.
sentences.r: Rezā nān o panir o gerdu mi-khorad.
sentences.en: Reza eats bread, cheese and walnuts.

sentences.fa: مینا نان و کره و عسل دوست دارد.
sentences.r: Minā nān o kare o 'asal dust dārad.
sentences.en: Mina likes bread, butter and honey.
Tom asks: "What is an Iranian breakfast?"

sentences.fa: رضا می‌گوید: «همه چیز، با یک استکان چای!»
sentences.r: Rezā mi-guyad: «hame chiz, bā yek estekān chāy!»
sentences.en: Reza says: "Everything – with a glass of tea!"

sentences.fa: تام یک لقمه‌ی بزرگ درست می‌کند: نان، پنیر، گردو، کره، عسل و تخم‌مرغ!
sentences.r: Tām yek loghme-ye bozorg dorost mi-konad: nān, panir, gerdu, kare, 'asal o tokhm-e-morgh!
sentences.en: Tom makes a big bite: bread, cheese, walnuts, butter, honey and egg!

vocab.en: sofreh (a cloth spread for a meal)
a bite; a little roll of bread with something inside

options: a big bite with everything in it

after: Bread, white cheese and walnuts – نان و پنیر و گردو – with sweet tea is the classic Iranian breakfast, and many families add butter and honey, jam, dates or fresh herbs. Breakfast is often eaten on a سفره, a cloth spread on the carpet. A لقمه is a little roll of flatbread wrapped around cheese and walnut (or anything else); Iranian mothers make لقمه for their children to take to school, and لقمه‌ی بزرگ 'a big bite' is a bit of a joke at the table. Notice the word order in رضا نان و پنیر و گردو می‌خورد: the verb comes last, and و 'and' (pronounced o) can join every item in a list.
